AGENDA
  GLENDALE CITY COUNCIL
  (STAFF ACCESS ONLY) MUNICIPAL SERVICES BUILDING
  633 E. Broadway, Room 105 (MSB 105)
  Glendale, CA 91206
 Welcome to Glendale City Hall. Meetings are broadcast live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and
 rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the
 proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office. Meetings are also archived on the
 City Website for viewing anytime at http://www.glendaleca.gov/government/agendas-minutes. If you
 have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City
 Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM
 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  JUNE 16, 2020

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Glendale City Council meeting will be available to the public
electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6 and AT&T U-verse Channel 99.
Streaming Online: https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

  and June 2, 2020
  b. Glendale Water and Power, re: Amendment No. 2 to Master Services Agreement
  (Contract No. C106259) with Itron, Inc. for Hardware and Software Support, and
  Maintenance and Professional Services
  1. Motion authorizing an Amendment to the Master Services Agreement (Contract No.
  C106259) with Itron Inc. for one-time professional services to support GWP’s upgrade to
  version 10.0 of the Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) and Itron Enterprise Edition
  (IEE) Meter Data Management System (MDMS), for an amount not to exceed $247,500,
  and for five years of continued hardware and software support and maintenance and
  enhanced technology and maintenance services for GWP’s AMI and MDMS for an
  amount not to exceed $2,148,909, for a total Amendment amount not to exceed
  $2,396,409. Upon expiration of the five-year software and hardware support and
  maintenance term, the City Council hereby authorizes the City Manager, or her
  designee, to execute one or more amendments to the MSA to provide continued
  hardware and software support and maintenance, and enhanced technology and
  maintenance services for the life of the hardware and software, if the funds for the
  continued maintenance support, updates, upgrades and licensing of the software and
  hardware are budgeted within the electric fund and/or water fund, as applicable, and if
  approved by the City Council as part of the annual citywide budget process
  c. Glendale Water and Power, re: Amendment No. 3 to the Software License and
  Support Services Agreement with Dominion Voltage, Inc. (DVI) for the Advanced
  Metering Infrastructure-based Conservation Voltage Reduction Program for Glendale
  Water & Power (GWP)
  1. Motion authorizing Amendment No. 3 to the Support Services Agreement (Contract No.
  C105540A) with Dominion Voltage, Inc. (DVI) to extend the Conservation Voltage
  Reduction program for Glendale Water & Power for a three-year term for an amount not
  to exceed $119,829 in year one, $122,944 in year two, and $126,141 in year three for a
  total not-to-exceed cost of $368,914. Upon expiration of the three-year term, the City
  Council hereby authorizes the City Manager, or her designee, to execute one or more
  amendments to the Support Services Agreement to provide continued software support
  and maintenance for the life of the software, if the funds for the continued maintenance
  support, updates, upgrades and licensing of the software are budgeted within the
  Electric fund, and approved by the City Council as part of the annual citywide budget
  process
  d. Libraries, Art, and Culture, re: Renewal of Contract for Integrated Library System
  Services
  1. Motion authorizing the City Manager or a designee to execute an amendment to the
  existing contract with Innovative Interfaces, Inc., to renew the contract for an additional
  5 years, for continuation of Integrated Library System Services for a total contract not-
  to-exceed amount of $461,550.45

 5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Council Member Najarian announced that the 24-hour fitness in Glendale will permanently
  close and asked staff to find a suitable business interested in occupying the property.

  Council Member Devine appointed Sue Bell Yank for the Arts and Culture Commission. She
  asked to adjourn the meeting in memory of Jerry Rankin.

  Council Member Kassakhian asked staff to provide a report on the usage of fields for
  organized sports and information on summer camps. Director of Community Services and
  Parks Onnig Bulanikian provided the information.

  Council Member Brotman announced that Glendale Community College is holding online
  sessions regarding deconstructing racism and asked staff to push the agenda to the public.
  He asked staff for the following actions: a deep dive on policing policies and practices; a
  reply to the letter received by Council from Civic Sundays, YWCA, and Black in Glendale;
  and answers to where the city stands regarding Attorney General Becerra’s proposed set of
  reforms on the use of force policies. He suggested to bring these items into a public
  discussion through a town hall meeting. Mr. Brotman asked staff to look into a program on
  Glendale’s historic legacy as a Sundown Town and how it played out into who we are today.
  On a different topic, he stated that he is concerned on the pace of progress on the clean
  energy alternatives to Grayson Power Plant. He asked staff to provide a status report.
  Seconded by Kassakhian.

  As a Glendale Committee Member, City Treasurer Raffi Manoukian provided a report on the
  Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy Advisory Committee meeting.
